U.S. And China Reach Trade Deal Including Loosened Controls On Crucial Rare Earths, Trump Says
By
Ty Roush
,
Forbes Staff
and
Sara Dorn
,
Forbes Staff.
Follow Authors
Jun 11, 2025, 08:54am EDT
Jun 11, 2025, 10:43am EDT
Share
Save
Comment
Topline
President Donald Trump on Wednesday said the U.S. reached a trade agreement with China, including a reprieve of restrictions China had imposed on rare earth minerals and magnets crucial to operations in industries from defense to auto.
The trade agreement includes full magnets and “any necessary rare earths” from China as the U.S. makes concessions on student visas.
Getty Images
Key Facts
Trump, in a
post
on Truth Social, said a deal was “done” between the U.S. and China, which he said will supply “any necessary rare earths” and magnets as the U.S. makes concessions on allowing Chinese students to attend American universities.
China imposed limitations on exports of rare earth minerals and magnets crucial to development of advanced defense technology, cars, robotics and more, in April amid the months-long tit-for-tat trade war with the U.S.
Though the details of the deal were unclear, some analysts predicted China wouldn’t give up the upper-hand after its rare earth restrictions prompted Ford Motor and some other U.S. companies to slow down production: “China’s going to want to maintain leverage,” Gracelin Baskaran, director of the critical minerals security program at the Center for Strategic and International Studies in Washington, told The
Wall Street Journal
, adding China’s position “puts American companies at direct risk given that any sort of agreements that have been made can be reneged on.”
Trump also said the U.S. would impose 55% tariffs on Chinese goods, while China would impose a 10% tax on U.S. imports.
Trump said a deal is subject to final approval from him and Chinese President Xi Jinping.
Chinese state media said earlier Wednesday Beijing had reached a “framework” for an agreement with the U.S. during talks in London.
Crucial Quote
Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick described the agreement as a “handshake for a framework” late Tuesday, indicating the terms were in flux: “Once that's done, we will be back on the phone together and we will begin to implement this agreement,” he said.
What To Watch For
The U.S. and Mexico are also nearing a deal to lift the 50% tariffs the U.S. imposed on Mexican steel imports, Bloomberg reported, citing people familiar with the talks.
Tangent
Shortly after China imposed the rare earth export limitations in April, Elon Musk said they had affected development of Tesla’s AI-powered Optimus robots. Musk said on an earnings call in April that Beijing was seeking “some assurances that these are not used for military purposes, which obviously they’re not.”
Key Background
Trump and Xi spoke in a 90-minute phone call Thursday, indicating the two sides were nearing a final agreement, weeks after they reached an initial deal in Geneva last month to pause tariffs that effectively cut off trade between the two superpowers for 90 days. U.S. officials expressed concerns, however, that Beijing continued to impose export restrictions on rare earth minerals and magnets despite the truce, prompting the U.S. to limit semiconductor exports from companies such as Nvidia. China initially imposed the export restrictions in April on seven types of rare earth metals and magnets made from three of them.
Big Number
90%. That’s the share of the world’s rare earths processed in China, which also makes about 90% of the world’s supply of rare earth magnets, according to
The New York Times.
